title: Cup and Cap Topological Neural Network
authors: Marta Niedostatek, Ferran Hernandez Caralt, Runyue Wang, Federica Baccini, Lorenzo Giambagli, Pietro Lió, Ginestra Bianconi
abstract: Topological Deep Learning (TDL) is designed to learn features associated with higher-dimensional simplices including not only nodes but also edges, triangles and so on. However, most TDL approaches, being based on boundary operators and Hodge Laplacians, have the limitation that features and signals cannot be lifted or lowered across more than one dimension per layer. To overcome this limitation, in this work, we propose the adoption of the cup and cap products. Specifically, we formulate the Cup and Cap Topological Neural Network (CCNN), a topological deep learning architecture designed to learn node-based variables (or 0-cochains) by taking into account their many-body interactions (e.g. triangles) present in the data. We validate CCNN by assessing its performance on the TopoBench datasets, revealing its competitiveness with respect to other simplicial complex neural networks.
summary: This paper introduces the Cup and Cap Topological Neural Network (CCNN), an advanced TDL architecture designed to overcome the dimensional limitations of prior methods. By employing cup and cap products, CCNN can effectively incorporate high-order topological information (like triangles) to learn node features. It demonstrates superior or competitive performance against existing state-of-the-art models on standard benchmark datasets.
main_problem: Existing Topological Deep Learning (TDL) methods are limited in their ability to propagate features across more than one dimension per layer using standard boundary operators.
main_result: The proposed Cup and Cap Topological Neural Network (CCNN) successfully learns node-based variables by incorporating many-body interactions (like triangles), achieving state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance on TopoBench datasets.
method: The CCNN utilizes the mathematical framework of cup and cap products, which act as lifting and lowering operators, respectively, allowing feature propagation across an arbitrary number of dimensions per layer.
model_or_system: The model is a Topological Neural Network (TNN) designed to process information encoded in simplicial complexes (nodes, edges, triangles). It processes 0-cochains ($\hat{	heta}_0$) through multiple layers using recursive equations involving the cup and cap products.
key_observables: Performance metrics (e.g., accuracy) on node-level tasks tested across various TopoBench datasets (Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, etc.).
important_parameters: The structure of the simplicial complex (up to triangles, $M=2$), the choice of auxiliary cochain formulation ($\eta$ or $\omega$), and hyperparameters like learning rates and hidden dimensions.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that cup and cap products provide the necessary mathematical machinery to overcome the dimensional limitations inherent in boundary/Hodge Laplacian approaches.
figures_summary: The notes reference Table 1, Table 2, Table 3, and Table 4, which summarize performance comparisons, architectural components (A, B, C terms), and ablation study results across different datasets.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the limitation of prior TDL methods. It then introduces the CCNN using cup and cap products. The methodology details the recursive construction of the network layers. Finally, the performance is validated through extensive benchmarking on the TopoBench library and ablation studies on specific datasets.
why_interesting: While the focus is on machine learning, the underlying mathematical machinery (simplicial complexes, cohomology, cup/cap products) is deeply rooted in algebraic topology, which has connections to quantum field theory and topological quantum computation.
